Primary outcomes were total adverse events (AEs), gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic and bleeding events.
Ibuprofen was not associated with a statistically significant difference in the risk of any adverse event compared with acetaminophen (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.36-1.79; I2 = 2.9%).
reason: Ibuprofen is an explicitly evaluated intervention with directly reported comparative safety outcomes. The comparison with acetaminophen evaluates ibuprofen itself, rather than a combination regimen or an entity shared by both arms. This is direct evidence, although the abstract notes limited certainty.

title: Comparative efficacy and thyroid function effects of non-surgical treatments for benign thyroid nodules: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
evidence_quotes: RCTs evaluating levothyroxine (L-T4), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation (MWA), percutaneous ethanol injection (PEI), or percutaneous laser ablation (PLA) in adults with BTN were included.
Outcomes were nodule volume, TSH, FT3, and FT4.
L-T4 showed strongest TSH suppression (vs. MWA: WMD≈-1.59, 95% CI: -2.42 to -0.79).

It is not merely mentioned or evaluated only within a combination regimen. The reported comparison supports attribution to levothyroxine, although the abstract notes limitations in clinical applicability.

title: Comparative bioavailability of sublingual vs. oral levothyroxine in patients with post-thyroidectomy hypothyroidism: A single-dose pilot study.
evidence_quotes: To evaluate the relative bioavailability of sublingual vs. oral levothyroxine (L-T4) in post-thyroidectomy patients, aiming to overcome gastrointestinal absorption variability.
Participants received a single 700-μg L-T4 dose under fasting conditions.
Pharmacokinetic parameters, including baseline-corrected AUC, Cmax and Tmax, were determined via noncompartmental analysis.
reason: Levothyroxine is the primary intervention, and its pharmacokinetic outcomes are directly measured. However, both groups receive levothyroxine; the comparison evaluates administration route rather than an effect attributable to levothyroxine itself. This supports indirect inclusion as route-comparison evidence.

title: Early Enteral Levothyroxine as Rescue Therapy in Cardiac Surgery Patients With Delayed Neurologic Recovery: A Randomized Trial.
evidence_quotes: Participants were randomized to receive either enteral levothyroxine (25-50 µg/d, titrated by body mass index) or an identical placebo from postoperative day 2 until intensive care unit (ICU) discharge.

The levothyroxine group (n = 35) showed significantly greater neurologic recovery (adjusted mean difference [aMD] in GCS score, +7.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.24-10.38; p < 0.001) with a 128% faster recovery rate (p < 0.001).
Given the small number of events (n = 21), this finding should be considered exploratory.
reason: Although described as rescue therapy, levothyroxine is the randomized primary intervention, not an incidental rescue medication. The placebo-controlled comparison directly evaluates its effects on neurologic recovery and other measured outcomes, permitting attribution to levothyroxine itself. The mortality finding is explicitly exploratory.

title: Peripheral endothelial and coronary microvascular responses to lipophilic versus hydrophilic ACE inhibitors in newly diagnosed hypertension.
evidence_quotes: In a controlled crossover trial, 33 hypertensive patients received eight weeks of quinapril (10 mg/day) and lisinopril (10 mg/day), separated by a washout period.
Brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and coronary flow reserve (CFR) were assessed via transthoracic Doppler echocardiography at baseline and after each treatment.
Both treatments effectively lowered blood pressure and improved FMD and CFR from baseline ( P  < 0.05).
reason: Lisinopril was directly evaluated as a separate treatment in a crossover trial, with blood pressure, endothelial function, and coronary microvascular outcomes measured after treatment. The washout-separated treatment periods support isolated attribution rather than combination-only or shared-both-arms classification.

title: Safety and tolerability of the ACE-inhibitor lisinopril among Nigerian adults with HIV: preliminary pilot data from a randomized clinical trial.
evidence_quotes: We report preliminary safety and tolerability data from 66 persons living with HIV (PLWH) (≥ 18 years old) who received escalating dosages of lisinopril or matched placebo, in addition to antiretroviral therapy in northern Nigeria.
Among 33 participants on lisinopril, 14 (42.4%) remained on 5 mg/day while 19 (57.6%) tolerated ≥ 10 mg/day.
Hypotension was most frequent in the Lisinopril group (4 (12.1%) vs. 2 (6.1%) in placebo), occurring at 10 mg.
reason: Lisinopril is the randomized intervention, with directly measured tolerability and adverse-event outcomes versus matched placebo. Antiretroviral therapy is background treatment; the randomized lisinopril-versus-placebo comparison isolates the effect of adding lisinopril.

title: Postpartum management of the hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence_quotes: In 9 trials (n=865) of antihypertensive (4 types) vs another (3 types) for nonsevere hypertension, additional antihypertensive need was similar in comparisons with either nifedipine or methyldopa, but greater when amlodipine or either enalapril or lisinopril/thiazide were compared with nifedipine.

title: Angiotensin II regulates anxiety and social-affective top-down and bottom-up attention control in a sex-dependent manner.
evidence_quotes: We conducted a preregistered, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pharmacological eye-tracking study in 79 healthy adults (males and females) and determined effects of transient AT1R blockade via losartan (50 mg) on emotional attention control using a validated anti-saccade paradigm with social (emotional faces) and non-social stimuli.
Losartan reduced state anxiety irrespective of sex but induced sexually dimorphic effects on attentional control.

In females, losartan enhanced performance by reducing endpoint error without altering latency. Conversely, in males, losartan increased endpoint error and prolonged latency of the first correct saccade.
reason: Losartan is the primary intervention in a randomized placebo-controlled study that directly measures anxiety and attentional-control outcomes. The reported comparison attributes effects to losartan itself, rather than a combination regimen.

title: Losartan with add-on spironolactone for severe COVID-19 in the intensive care unit: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_quotes: The experimental group received standard care plus losartan and conditional addition of spironolactone for 10 days while the control group received standard care alone.
We found no significant difference in median SOFA-score on day 7 between the groups (3 vs 2; p = 0.5).
This trial did not detect a statistically significant treatment effect of losartan, with spironolactone added in a minority of patients, on clinical outcomes in COVID-19 ICU patients.

title: The renin angiotensin system in cognitive flexibility: Effects of single-dose losartan on task-switching in healthy volunteers.
evidence_quotes: Participants were randomly assigned a single 50 mg dose of losartan, an angiotensin type 1 receptor blocker, or placebo.
While participants on losartan exhibited numerically superior RTs and accuracy, losartan did not significantly improve task-switching relative to placebo.
An exploratory probe suggested that losartan improved accuracy on direction-switch trials, indicating a potential drug effect under specific cognitive conditions.

The overall null result does not diminish its relevance as direct evidence; the direction-switch accuracy finding was exploratory.

title: Sex differences in the risk of metformin-associated gastrointestinal adverse events: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence_quotes: Eligible studies reported metformin-associated GIAEs separately in females and males, while studies in which GIAEs could not be attributed to metformin were excluded.
Females had significantly higher odds of metformin-associated GIAEs than males (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.58-2.17), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses.

title: Impact of Metformin Plus Lifestyle Intervention Compared With Lifestyle Intervention Alone on Prediabetes Remission in Participants With Impaired Glucose Regulation: The China DPP Study.
evidence_quotes: They received either metformin plus lifestyle intervention or lifestyle intervention alone for 2 years.

title: Breaking the cycle of loneliness: A randomized controlled trial of the anti-inflammatory naproxen in lonely, middle-aged adults.
evidence_quotes: Participants took naproxen (400 mg; n=40 analyzed) or placebo (n=42 analyzed) daily for 2 weeks, completing a baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up session (2 weeks post-intervention).
There were no significant treatment by time effects on any of the outcomes, except for inflammatory gene expression, which decreased in the naproxen-treated group.
Those with the highest baseline stress reported reductions in loneliness and anhedonia in the naproxen group.

title: Comparing Trypsin-Chymotrypsin and Naproxen Sodium for Post-Endodontic Treatment Pain: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
evidence_quotes: A total of 100 patients were randomly allocated to receive oral formulations of the trypsin-chymotrypsin group (n = 50) or the naproxen sodium group (n = 50).
The numeric rating scale (NRS) was utilised to assess pain score at 1, 6, 12, and 24-hour intervals.

Pain scores were comparable at 1-hour intervals (p = 0.695); however, at 6 hours, the trypsin-chymotrypsin group showed a significant reduction in pain compared with the naproxen sodium group (p = 0.049).

Single time point pantoprazole MRs measured in plasma between 4 and 8 h after pantoprazole administration were sufficient for accurate CYP2C19 phenotyping by demonstrating significant and robust correlations to the AUC0-8h MR 5-hydroxyomeprazole/omeprazole with Spearman ρ ≥ 0.8.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of omeprazole for preventing esophageal stricture in patients with Zargar grade 2b and 3a corrosive esophageal injuries: A trial-based economic evaluation.
evidence_quotes: Twenty patients were randomized to receive either standard treatment alone (n = 10) or standard treatment plus omeprazole (n = 10).

The incidence of corrosive esophageal stricture was 20% (2/10) in the omeprazole group and 70% (7/10) in the standard treatment group (relative risk, 0.29; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-1.05; Fisher's exact test, P = .070).
Omeprazole plus standard treatment reduced healthcare costs by THB 4642.30 per patient from the provider perspective and THB 5476.60 per patient from the patient perspective.

title: Antidepressant effects of facial botulinum toxin a injections: Insights from randomized controlled trials.
evidence_quotes: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of facial injections of Botulinum toxin A (BoNT/A) compared with placebo and the active antidepressant sertraline.
Subgroup analysis revealed that BoNT/A was superior to placebo (SMD = -1.04) and demonstrated efficacy comparable to sertraline (SMD = -0.23).
While overall adverse event rates were similar to controls (RR = 1.04), BoNT/A was associated with transient local reactions, avoiding the systemic side effects observed with sertraline.

It is not merely a background mention or part of a combination regimen. Include as indirect evidence because the review focuses on BoNT/A and evaluates sertraline as a comparator.

title: PTSD treatment impacts on pain: secondary analysis of sertraline, prolonged exposure, and their combination.
evidence_quotes: This secondary analysis of a PTSD effectiveness trial examined the impact of PTSD treatments on pain complaints in 196 veterans randomized to three conditions: Prolonged Exposure plus placebo (PE + PLB), PE + Sertraline (PE + SERT), and SERT with enhanced medication management, overall and among those who reported clinically significant pain at baseline.
The PE + PLB group showed greater reductions in pain interference during treatment than SERT and PE + SERT.
While it is uncertain reduced pain was due to the treatments themselves, lower scores for all treatments suggest that PTSD-focused treatments may reduce pain even without a specific pain focus.
reason: Sertraline is a randomized intervention with directly measured pain outcomes, both in a standalone pharmacotherapy arm with medication management and combined with prolonged exposure. title: Effect of continuation treatment on health-related quality of life in remitted psychotic depression.

title: Effect of simvastatin versus calcium hydroxide intracanal medications on postoperative pain and cytokine modulation in symptomatic apical periodontitis: a randomized controlled trial.

Both medications reduced cytokine levels from baseline; however, intergroup comparisons showed no significant differences.

title: Simvastatin Treatment in Patients with Liver Cirrhosis: A Phase II Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial Shows Reduction in IL6 Levels.
evidence_quotes: This multicenter randomized double-blinded, placebo-controlled phase II trial of 40 mg/day oral simvastatin to reduce the likelihood of hepatocarcinogenesis was conducted at four sites in the United States.
Serum IL6 levels, detectable in all participants, decreased significantly in the simvastatin group compared with the placebo group (P = 0.02).

In this randomized controlled trial, simvastatin was well tolerated in patients with liver cirrhosis but did not result in a decrease in AFP-L3%, potentially owing to the low number of participants with detectable AFP/AFP-L3%.
reason: Simvastatin was the randomized intervention evaluated against placebo, with directly measured biomarker and safety outcomes attributable to simvastatin. IL6 decreased, while the primary AFP-L3% endpoint did not. This is direct evidence for simvastatin in cirrhosis, but not evidence of reduced liver cancer incidence.

title: Effect of Simvastatin on Success of Pulpotomy in Carious Permanent Molars With Symptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
evidence_quotes: The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of simvastatin (SMV) in combination with alpha tricalcium phosphate (αTCP) as pulpotomy agents in cariously exposed permanent mandibular molars with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis.
Sixty patients were randomly assigned equally to either the SMV-αTCP or MTA group.
No significant difference in success rates was found between the SMV-αTCP (92.5%) and MTA (96.2%) groups (p > 0.05).

However, it is evaluated only in combination with alpha tricalcium phosphate against MTA, so the comparison cannot isolate simvastatin's effect. This is indirect combination-regimen evidence, not direct evidence attributable to simvastatin alone.

title: Prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) vs. non-PCC strategies for warfarin reversal in left ventricular assist device recipients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence_quotes: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing PCC with non-PCC strategies for warfarin reversal in LVAD recipients.

In head-to-head comparisons, PCC achieved faster INR correction than non-PCC comparators (mean difference - 7.6 h; p = 0.001) and required fewer FFP units (-2.6 units; p = 0.019), with no significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 1.14; p = 0.490) or thrombotic events (RR 1.43; p = 0.176).

title: Calciphylaxis in chronic kidney disease: a systematic review of pathomechanisms and risk factors for calcific uremic arteriolopathy.
evidence_quotes: We searched EMBASE and PubMed up to February 2026, reviewing all studies that would facilitate a comparison of CKD patients with and without CUA.

The factors that consistently emerged related to CUA were decreased albumin, higher alkaline phosphatase, diabetes, increased body mass index, female sex, vitamin K antagonist (VKA) use, increased calcium phosphate product, and calcification and thrombosis in subcutaneous small arteries.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of apixaban and rivaroxaban versus warfarin in atrial fibrillation patients with end-stage renal disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: The correlation between cardiac T2*MRI and B-Type natriuretic peptides in patients with transfusion-dependent anemias and systemic iron overload: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Bimekizumab in patients with active psoriatic arthritis and previous inadequate response or intolerance to tumour necrosis factor-α inhibitors: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial (BE COMPLETE).

116 (43%) of 267 patients receiving bimekizumab reached ACR50, compared with nine (7%) of 133 patients receiving placebo (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 11·1 [95% CI 5·4-23·0], p<0·0001).
Treatment-emergent adverse events up to week 16 were reported in 108 (40%) of 267 patients receiving bimekizumab and 44 (33%) of 132 patients receiving placebo.
reason: Bimekizumab is the randomized primary intervention, with directly measured joint, skin, and safety outcomes versus placebo. The reported comparison attributes outcomes to bimekizumab itself rather than to a combination regimen or treatment shared by both arms.

title: Network meta-analyses comparing the efficacy of biologic treatments for achieving complete resolution of nail psoriasis at 24-28 and 48-52 weeks.
evidence_quotes: Bayesian NMAs were performed using a generalized linear model with a logit link to model the binary outcome of nail clearance at weeks 24-28 and 48-52.

For the NMA at weeks 24-28, which included seven biologics and placebo, the absolute probability of achieving complete resolution of NP was highest for ixekizumab (46.4%; 95% credibility interval [CrI] 35.2-58.0), followed by brodalumab (37.1%; 95% CrI 17.1-62.2) and bimekizumab (30.3%; 95% CrI 12.7-53.9).
reason: Bimekizumab is explicitly evaluated as a treatment in the network meta-analysis, with a treatment-specific estimate for complete nail psoriasis resolution at weeks 24–28. This is entity-specific efficacy evidence, not merely a background mention or a combination-regimen result.

title: Efficacy and safety of bimekizumab in the treatment of psoriatic arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence_quotes: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of bimekizumab in the management of PsA.
Bimekizumab significantly increased the rates of PASI75 and PASI100 compared with placebos [RR = 7.22, 95% CI (5.24, 9.94), p < 0.001; RR = 10.12, 95% CI (6.00, 17.09), p < 0.001].
The rate of overall adverse events was slightly higher in the bimekizumab group [RR = 1.42, 95% CI (1.05, 1.93) p = 0.023).
reason: This systematic review and meta-analysis directly evaluates bimekizumab against placebo in psoriatic arthritis and reports efficacy and safety outcomes attributable to bimekizumab.

title: Short-term efficacy of biologics in moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa: A systematic review and NMA.
evidence_quotes: To assess the relative efficacy of approved biologic therapies (bimekizumab 320 mg every 2 weeks [Q2W], secukinumab 300 mg Q2W and every 4 weeks [Q4W] and adalimumab 40 mg every week [QW]) at Week 12-16 in moderate-to-severe HS.

Bimekizumab ranked as the most efficacious treatment across all predefined efficacy outcomes in both predominantly biologic-naïve and biologic-experienced networks, showing consistent response levels.
In the predominantly biologic-naïve network, bimekizumab Q2W compared with secukinumab (Q4W) demonstrated significantly higher odds of response for all HiSCR outcomes
reason: Bimekizumab is explicitly evaluated as an individual treatment, with entity-specific efficacy estimates for hidradenitis suppurativa outcomes. Although comparisons are synthesized through a network meta-analysis rather than head-to-head trials, the evidence directly addresses bimekizumab and is not limited to a combination regimen or shared treatment.

title: Bimekizumab efficacy in scalp, nail and palmoplantar psoriasis versus comparators and over 4 years.
evidence_quotes: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis and scalp/palmoplantar Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score ≥3 or modified Nail Psoriasis Severity Index (mNAPSI) >10 at baseline were randomized to bimekizumab or comparators (adalimumab, ustekinumab, secukinumab, placebo).

At Week 24, rates of complete resolution of scalp/nail/palmoplantar psoriasis were 77.7%/39.8%/78.7% with bimekizumab and 58.1%/24.5%/73.3% with adalimumab; at Week 52, 71.9%/54.0%/85.2% with bimekizumab and 51.8%/30.6%/75.0% with ustekinumab; and at Week 48, 80.6%/69.5%/82.4% with bimekizumab and 71.6%/52.5%/76.8% with secukinumab.
Complete scalp/nail/palmoplantar clearance rates were sustained through 4 years' bimekizumab treatment (79.5%/61.6%/88.7%).
reason: Bimekizumab is the explicitly evaluated primary intervention, with directly measured psoriasis clearance outcomes against named comparators and during long-term treatment. The reported randomized comparisons evaluate bimekizumab itself rather than a combination regimen or an intervention shared by both arms.

title: A randomized, crossover study to evaluate α-tocopherol bioavailability via a microemulsion gel or dry tablet delivery in healthy adults.
evidence_quotes: Vitamin E (α-tocopherol) is an essential micronutrient for human health and optimal physiological function.

Twelve participants (age  =  37.3  ±  9.6 years; height  =  173.4  ±  11.8 cm; body mass  =  71.2  ±  10.0 kg) participated in a double-blind, randomized, crossover trial comparing two delivery methods both dosed at 288 mg of α-tocopherol.

The microemulsion gel formula delivery demonstrated significantly greater area under the curve (p < 0.001) and serum concentration maximums (p  =  0.003) for serum α-tocopherol compared to the tablet delivery.
reason: The study directly measures vitamin E bioavailability, but both conditions deliver the same α-tocopherol dose. The reported differences evaluate delivery formulations rather than an isolated effect of vitamin E, making this useful indirect evidence.

title: Racial and Ethnic Disparity in Preference-Weighted Quality of Life: Findings from the Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial.
evidence_quotes: Selenium and vitamin E cancer prevention trial participants who completed the SF-6D at baseline, and in at least 1 of follow-up years 1, 3, and 5 were included.
This study compared mean SF-6D scores across race/ethnicity at each point using a linear mixed model controlling for demographic and clinical characteristics.
The results suggest there is a preference-weighted HRQOL difference by race/ethnicity that cannot be explained by social and clinical variables alone.
reason: Vitamin E appears in the name of the source trial, but this analysis evaluates quality-of-life differences by race/ethnicity, not outcomes by vitamin E exposure or assignment. It therefore provides no measured vitamin E-specific outcome.

title: What is the dietary intake and nutritional status of defence members: a systematic literature review.
evidence_quotes: Therefore, this review assessed the diets of military populations against national nutritional guidelines and Military Dietary Reference Intakes (MDRI).
Results also indicated suboptimal intake of fibre, essential fatty acids, vitamin A, vitamin E, folate, Mg, Zn and iodine.
reason: Vitamin E appears in a list of nutrients with suboptimal dietary intake. The abstract does not evaluate it as an intervention, an outcome-linked exposure, or a comparator. Reporting intake inadequacy does not establish evidence of vitamin E's effects.

title: Effects of Differing Nutritional Supplementation Combined With High-Intensity Aerobic Interval Training on Functional Exercise Capacity, Cardiac Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Randomized Trial.
evidence_quotes: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to compare the effects of two nutritional supplementation strategies Amendcor (creatine, D-ribose, coenzyme Q10, and vitamin E) versus biquinol+D-ribose, combined with a 12-wk group-based high-intensity aerobic interval training on functional exercise capacity, health-related quality of life, left ventricular ejection fraction, and perceived exertion, in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

RESULTS: Study participants supplemented with creatine + D-ribose+ CoQ10 + Vit. E demonstrated significantly greater improvements in functional exercise capacity (6-min walk test: +19.88%, VO₂ peak: +25.46%, perceived exertion: -38.53%), health-related quality of life: -25.64%, left ventricular ejection fraction: +40.94%, compared with subjects supplemented with ubiquinol + D-ribose ( P  < 0.05).
reason: Vitamin E is explicitly included in a randomized intervention with measured clinical and functional outcomes. However, it is evaluated only within a multi-ingredient supplement combined with exercise training. The comparison cannot isolate vitamin E's contribution, so this is indirect combination-regimen evidence rather than direct evidence of vitamin E's effect.

title: Evidence on Glutathione and Boosters for Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
evidence_quotes: N-acetylcysteine (odds ratio [OR] 0.19, 95% credible intervals [CrI] 0.05-0.63), GSH (OR 0.34, 95% CrI 0.13-0.79) and vitamin E (OR 0.33, 95% CrI 0.11-0.91) were associated with a reduced incidence of grade 3/4 CIPN compared with placebo.
These findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with pre-existing neuropathy but were not retained in analyses restricted to double-blind studies.
reason: Vitamin E is explicitly evaluated as an intervention against placebo, with a separately reported effect on severe chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy. This is direct, entity-specific evidence rather than a background mention or combination-regimen effect. The reported association is preliminary and was not retained in analyses restricted to double-blind studies.
